messages.subject: Re: Processing Axivity Data in GGIR
messages.body_plain:
Hi Claire,

You treat .cwa files exactly the same as .gt3x or .csv files, to the extent that you can put both types of files into the same directory and it will run both fine.
Just a note from a very experienced Axivity user - The cwa files take 2/3 times longer as they are converted in R prior to generating the part 1 meta files. After that they are the same speed :).

Kind regards,
Ben

messages.body_plain:
Hi Clair,

If you only specified mode = 1, then you would indeed not expect any output files. Instrady you would find an empty folder structure with only the GGIR part 1 milestone data.

Regarding the speed of reading in gt3x and cwa: It may be worth highlighting that this is not direct a property of the accelerometer brands as such, but mainly driven by the open-source software used to read in the data. For gt3x we have been lucky that the open-source software is faster than the code we have for cwa.

If you think GGIR is too slow at reading in .cwa or any other data format then I think there is a good chance we can speed it up. In relation to GENEActiv bin files I am hoping to do some work on that this in the summer in collaboration with someone with more expertise in this area then myself. However, for Axivity I do not have an ongoing project for which I can easily justify working on this, yet. If you or someone else wants to work on this or has a budget to fund the effort then let me know.

Regards,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
> Also I have another question related to the cleaning: In our study some subjects did not provided enough sleep log for all the days recorded. I kept those days blank in the sleep log. The days without sleep logs cannot be reflected in the final night summaries and average summaries. I am retrieving the results from QC summaries and cleaning the days on my ends. Please let me know if you have a better idea.

Yes, I think you identified a good solution. GGIR provides two version of the output:
results folder: these are typically cleaned, which means that all days with do not meet inclusion criteria are removed, and if you use a sleeplog then all nights without a sleeplog will also be removed. I do this because I am not sure whether it is informative to mix two different sleep methods (with and without sleeplog) in the same person-level summary measures. In GGIR part 5 I have no been this strict about the availability of sleeplog method, because in GGIR part 5 is not on sleep assessment but on capturing the waking hours of the day.
QC folder: all days are included and it is up to you to clean and summarise the data as you prefer.

Approach 1 aims to be the easiest default approach relevant to most GGIR users. However, if you feel approach 2 better aligns with your research interests then yes definitely go for that. I created it, exactly because I knew there would be need for a less cleaned-up version of the data.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: warning messgages in final
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Can you post the call you made to GGIR, and the format of your sleep log?

The problem in warning 1 should be fairly obvious - `excludefirstlast` is used more than once. It shouldn't have caused any issues (unless they were different).

For warning 2, your sleep log needs to match the format given in the vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#233_Key_arguments_related_to_sleep_analysis>. You may also need to specify "colid" to tell GGIR which column has the ID number. If GGIR hasn't been able to use your sleep log, it will have fallen back to automatic sleep detection. You can check if this happened in your data by seeing if the variable "sleeplog_used" is zero (your sleeplog was not used) or one (it was used).

Taren
